sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tier-3/4 Server Rack Space Leasing and Bare-Metal Server Hosting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 10-18 (incorporation and articles), s. 74 (registered office); alternative federal incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s. 4 and s. 16
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), 610-10611 98 Avenue, Edmonton, AB T5K 1B5
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form AL-1) submitted via Corporate Registry Connect or paper filing
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued without par value and consideration may be cash, property, services or promissory notes. No escrow deposit required for ordinary business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The incorporation of the Company under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is ratified. The subscription for 100 common shares by the incorporating shareholder is accepted, and such shares are issued fully paid. The registered office of the Company is established at the address in the Articles of Incorporation, and a registered records keeper is appointed. The following officers are appointed: President, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. The directors are directed to open corporate bank accounts, file all required notices, and maintain corporate records in compliance with applicable law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – NUANS Name Search (via Corporate Registry Connect)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name to determine whether the name is distinguishable and available. If using a numbered company, obtain an incorporation number upon filing. Name reservations are valid for 90 days. File the reservation through the official portal or authorize a service provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, submit a new name search request for an alternative name, or proceed with a numbered company as a fallback.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), via Corporate Registry Connect or paper filing at 10611 102 ST, Edmonton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit Form AL-1 Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name (or number), share capital structure, restrictions on share transfers, registered office address, and names and addresses of first directors. Payment of the $120 CAD incorporation fee must accompany the filing. Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation under the ABCA.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (if not numbered)
Consent to Act as Director for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, comply with the Registry's deficiency notification by filing amendments or clarifications within 30 days; if the incorporation is rejected, correct the articles and re-submit with payment of applicable re-filing fee if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and By-Law Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board (or act by unanimous written resolution) to adopt by-laws, appoint senior officers (e.g., President, CFO, Corporate Secretary), select a fiscal year-end, authorize bank account opening, and approve the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Record the decisions in the minute book. Keep by-laws in the corporate records; file any prescribed form with the Registry if required by the ABCA.
required_dossiers: Notice or waiver of notice of meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is not attained or consent is incomplete, hold a second meeting with verified quorum or obtain written consent of all directors. Amend by-laws by subsequent board resolution if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records Keeper
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (for registered office updates); Corporation's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office address is physically located in Alberta and is open during statutory hours. Appoint or confirm the individual responsible for records (registered records keeper). Prepare and maintain corporate records at the registered office: articles, by-laws, minutes, share register, directors' register, and central securities register / beneficial ownership registry. If the initial office differs from the articles, file Form AL-13 Notice of Change of Registered Office.
required_dossiers: Share register and beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If records inspection fails, update the records immediately and file a corrective notice with the Registry; administrative penalties apply for persistent non-compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Regulatory Account Registration for Operational Start
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Alberta Corporate Registry / Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta (WCB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA for corporate income tax, GST/HST (if revenues exceed the $30,000 registration threshold or voluntary election), payroll (if employees), and import/export (if applicable). Register with the Alberta WCB for mandatory workers' compensation coverage if hiring employees; secure a municipal business licence if any. Use the BN for corporate tax filing under Alberta's Tax Administration Agreement.
required_dossiers: Form RC1 Request for a Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is in obvious error, file corrections with CRA Business Window; if the WCB classification is disputed, request reconsideration under section 3 of the Workers' Compensation Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Municipal Affairs (Safety Codes Council) and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating license; municipal development permit and building permit (Safety Codes Act compliance) govern physical data center operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no full EIA required for data center colocation; registration may apply for standby generator emissions or cooling tower discharge if above applicable thresholds)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and the Canadian Environmental Protection Act for VOCs; standby diesel generators must meet CCME emission limits and NSPS 40 CFR Part 60; wastewater discharge to municipal sewer shall conform to the Municipal Government Act and local sewer bylaw limits

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Safety Codes Act (fire code compliance), structural building occupancy permit, and workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act, including general safety inspections coordinated with local fire and building authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); GST/HST and corporate income tax administration; official portal: 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services/menu.html) and GST/HST NETFILE filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must obtain a Canadian Business Number (BN) and separate GST/HST registration program account. The procedure is: (1) determine if the entity makes taxable supplies in Canada or derives Canadian-source income; (2) submit CRA Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' in person, by mail, by fax, or if eligible via Business Registration Online (BRO); (3) indicate the GST/HST account type (RT) and, if required, a corporate income tax account (RC); (4) provide constitutional documents, foreign registration proof, a Canadian contact or authorized representative, and information on the appointed director(s) or resident agent if an Alberta provincial extra-provincial registration is needed; (5) if the small-supplier threshold is exceeded, registration becomes mandatory effective from the calendar day the threshold was surpassed; (6) CRA issues a 15-digit BN (program account suffix 'RT' or 'RC') typically within 10–15 business days; no share capital minimum is required for a Canada Business Corporations Act or Alberta Business Corporations Act corporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the corporation is a separate taxpayer under Part I of the Income Tax Act; there is no check-through or pass-through election for incorporated entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) a corporation may elect under subsection 216 of the Income Tax Act to report rental and timber royalty income on a net Part I tax basis rather than Part XIII withholding; (ii) a non-resident-owned investment corporation may, in limited cases, elect special status; (iii) for GST/HST purposes, closely related corporations may jointly elect under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act to treat supplies as having no consideration and thereby simplify net tax; (iv) simplified or quick method elections are available for smaller registrants; (v) hybrid mismatch rules under sections 18.2 and 18.3 of the Income Tax Act are mandatory, not elective; no check-the-box forms exist.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (including supplies of associated persons) in the current calendar quarter or in any preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration is mandatory for a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada unless the person qualifies as a small supplier; certain non-residents must register if they solicit orders in Canada or carry on business through a permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based e-invoicing system is currently in force in Canada. A GST/HST registrant must issue an invoice containing the prescribed particulars under section 221 of the Excise Tax Act, retain all books and records in Canada (or make them available electronically via a Canadian representative), and file GST/HST returns electronically using GST/HST NETFILE if the registrant uses the GST/HST Quick Method, is a monthly filer, or is otherwise required by CRA. Large filers may use XML/API EDI filing but there is no government pre-clearance of individual invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The zero-rating rules differ by supply type. For goods, the sale must be to an exporter (usually a non-resident) and the goods must be exported from Canada as part of the contract; evidence of export is required within the prescribed time. For services, section 23(1) of the Excise Tax Act zero-rates a supply made to a non-resident unless the service falls within a listed exception, including a service in respect of real property situated in Canada, a service in respect of tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or a service that is ancillary to the supply of the real property. A data center colocation arrangement that grants a leasehold interest in server rack space or floor space located in Canada is considered, in whole or in part, a supply of real property situated in Canada and will be taxable at 5% GST (no Alberta provincial sales tax). A separately invoiced and independently supplied bare-metal hosting service, where the dominant characteristic is the provision of computing infrastructure and not the use of Canadian real property, may qualify for zero-rating if supplied to a non-resident recipient who does not consume or use the service in Canada. Contractual wording, separate pricing, and invoicing must be carefully structured; CRA substance will govern.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or CBSA-approved equivalent when physical goods or servers are exported from Canada
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/ACH proof of payment evidencing the value settlement from the non-resident buyer

Signed commercial contract/lease agreement with non-resident recipient and documentary proof of the recipient's non-resident status (e.g., foreign registration documents, permanent establishment analysis)
Detailed invoice breakdown separating real property lease elements (taxable) from any export service elements (if zero-rated claimed)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess within four years from the date of the return; the period is unlimited for misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud. A fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating claim will result in full reassessment of GST at 5%, arrears interest, and penalties. Under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act, false statements or omissions in returns carry a penalty of up to 25% of the tax sought to be evaded; summary conviction fines range up to CAD 25,000, with higher fines available on indictment. Directors, officers, agents, or persons who participate in fraudulent zero-rating may incur joint and several personal liability. CRA also imposes gross-negligence penalties under subsection 163(2) of the Income Tax Act for corporate income tax errors. To mitigate clawbacks, the taxpayer must retain complete export evidence for six years and be prepared to defend the genuine export/non-resident service characterization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary and exchange-rate authority; banking supervision is discharged by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign-exchange administrative veto agency in the sense of a convertibility control board; cross-border payments are supervised by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), with policy oversight by the Department of Finance Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Exchange controls were dismantled in 1951 with the repeal of the Foreign Exchange Control Act; since then Canada has operated a free-floating currency regime and does not require prior approval for profit repatriation, debt service, or capital withdrawals by non-resident investors. Practical hurdles are fiscal rather than exchange-control: non-resident dividends, interest, royalties, and rents are generally subject to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, reduced by Canada-US and other tax treaties), and any transfer of funds over C$10,000 is captured by FINTRAC as a Large Cash/EFT Transaction Report or Cross-Border EFT Report. A data-center colocation lessor is a services/rent business, so convertibility risk is immaterial provided corporate tax compliance, GST/HST filings, and CRA information returns are current.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio. Invoice proceeds from colocation, managed hosting, and bandwidth services may be held in CAD, USD, or any freely accepted foreign currency; receipts must be translated into CAD for corporate tax purposes using the Bank of Canada daily average exchange rate or an acceptable functional-currency conversion rate, and underlying books and records must be retained for six years under Income Tax Act section 230. Exporters must nevertheless report cross-border electronic fund transfers exceeding C$10,000 to FINTRAC and comply with CRA/Canada Border Services Agency documentation rules when the contract is characterized as an export of services.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM — as auxiliary liquidity rails only. Non-bank fintech providers (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, etc.) may operate in Canada as FINTRAC-registered money services businesses (MSBs) or foreign MSBs for cross-border EFTs, but they are not chartered Schedule I banks and cannot credibly serve as the sole depository for an Alberta business corporation. Legal constraints: they must be registered under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and, once the retail payments framework is fully operative, may require payment service provider licensing under the Retail Payment Activities Act; a Canadian MSB cannot provide the 'banking' relationship expected by CRA for GST/HST, creditor, and lender purposes. Use them for collection of tenant/colocation invoices in foreign currency or low-value ACH-type inflows, with same-day settlement into the Schedule I account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person director appearance is generally required for foreign-owned or remotely managed Canadian corporations where the ultimate beneficial owner is not a Canadian tax resident. Whereas a Canadian-resident director may complete onboarding fully remotely with video verification for certain low-risk profiles, a non-resident director must either attend a Canadian branch in person, appear at a Canadian embassy/consulate-approved notary, or complete a live video KYC interview together with notarized corporate resolutions and source-of-funds evidence. The surest opening route for a colocation/lease vehicle is: (i) registered office and accounting agent in Calgary or Edmonton; (ii) one Canadian-resident authorized signatory; and (iii) a remote interview supported by legalized certificates for non-resident UBOs, because the bank's PEP/sanction screening window is the critical gating process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder/director domicile mismatched with Canadian registered office, exposing the account to classification as a 'non-Canadian business' under FINTRAC risk-based screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Alberta Certificate of Status, registered office consent, Canadian corporate registry extract (CORA), notarized director resolutions appointing an in-country authorized signatory, UBO declaration at the 25% threshold with ID/passport copies, source of funds evidence for capital injection, business plan, colocation lease master service agreement or rack-lease template, and client/tenant credit list.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Blocked or suspicious payment inflows sourced from unregulated crypto miners or high-risk merchant acquirers channeled into a colocation account, triggering FINTRAC Large EFT Reporting and account freezing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed colocation/tenant due-diligence policy, server-rack sub-lessee onboarding records, service invoices and payment references, AML risk-tier matrix showing Low_Risk_Standard classification for ISIC 6209, external IP-block assignment credentials, anti-crypto mining clause where adopted, board-approved sanctions screening procedure, and monthly transaction monitoring share with the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Liquidity fee/management fee outflows to a related parent or foreign shareholder flagged as conduit payments or deemed dividend that would attract Part XIII withholding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Section 85/85.1 rollover documentation where applicable, written intercompany services agreement with transfer-pricing benchmark report, CRA Form T106/T1134 filings if required, board minutes approving fee, GL breakdown separating invoice payment from capital distribution, and Part XIII withholding remittance receipts including the CRA NR601 filing or bank remittance transfer receipts unless nil.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: SWIFT MT103 credit from the parent/shareholder bank to the Canadian Schedule I bank account using the Canadian bank's SWIFT BIC and the Canadian institution-branch-account number (Canada does not use IBAN). Payment narrative should read: 'Capital subscription / paid-up capital — share consideration for CA_CORP.' No central-bank approval or export-surrender requirement applies; the bank will file the FINTRAC EFT report for transfers over C$10,000. The wire narrative must quote the shareholder and the allotment resolution; the corporation executes an allocation of consideration and issues share certificates for post-capital verification. GST/HST neutrality applies where the injection is equity rather than a lease payment; CRA and banks will ask for the share subscription agreement, valuation, and corporate authorization before releasing funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Regular trade disbursements for rack-lease refunds, equipment suppliers, subcontractors, overseas bandwidth providers, management fees, and distributions should clear through SWIFT MT103 for single customer credit transfers, MT202 COV for bank-to-bank movements where appropriate, and Payments Canada Lynx RTGS for same-day high-value CAD/USD interbank settlement; domestic tenant refunds settle via Automated Funds Transfer (EFT/ACH). These rails align with the target Monthly_ACH and Swift_Wire payment matrix. For data-center colocation, commercial letters of credit are uncommon unless procuring equipment or power infrastructure; a standby LC (SWIFT MT700/MT707) is recommended for tenant completion guarantees, with commercial invoices and delivery documents attached. All outgoing payments must carry payer/tax identifiers and be screened against OFAC/UN/EU sanctions by the relevant Canadian bank correspondent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot (T+2, CAD/USD pair via Schedule I dealing desk, no premium, collateral posted for margin).
Outright FX Forward (extendable, up to 12-month tenors for rent-roll FX exposure; eligible for hedge accounting under IFRS 9 when foreign-currency lease receivables are designated).

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for CAD vs exotic currencies such as BRL, IDR, and NGN — settlement in USD, no underlying principal delivery; must be transacted with a qualifying dealer and monitored under Alberta Derivatives Act trade reporting if thresholds are exceeded.
FX Swap (spot-forward combination in CAD/USD for short-term liquidity bridging between capital injection and capex drawdown).
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS or Cross-Currency Swap) where non-CAD debt or USD-denominated equipment finance is deployed; fixed-to-fixed or floating-to-floating.
Vanilla FX/Currency Option (call or put on USD receipts to protect downside while preserving upside; premium expensed under IFRS 9 as derivative positive fair value or hedging cost).

All instruments are permitted strictly for economic hedging of the colocation business and may not be used for speculative trading by an unregulated Canadian entity; execution must be under an ISDA/CSA master agreement and subject to CSA derivative trade reporting if end-user thresholds are exceeded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No graduated late fine; failure to file for 1 year triggers administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212; reinstatement requires assent of the Director, payment of CAD 25 reinstatement fee plus all arrears (CAD 12 per missed annual return); business capacity and banking access suspended during dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (ABCA s. 264 for provincial corporations; extra-provincial registration annual return where federally incorporated and registered in Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation (or registration for extra-provincial corporations) each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Certificate of Status marked 'non-compliant' immediately after the 60-day window; after 12 months of continuous default, Registrar may administratively dissolve the provincial corporation or cancel the extra-provincial registration; reinstatement costs CAD 100–200 plus all annual return arrears and may require Director's review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 6th month after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 year-end filed by June 30); balance-due day is 2/3 months after year-end depending on CCPC status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); doubled rates (10% + 2%/month) on repeated default; nil-filer sanctions of CAD 100 per failure for two consecutive years; failure to file after demand may trigger prosecution and director/personal liability for unpaid balances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Beneficial Ownership Transparency (BOT) Registry Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrent with the Alberta annual return filing window (anniversary-based)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate registry filing fee, but non-filing or false filing under the BOT Act exposes the reporting company and its directors/officers to administrative penalties up to CAD 200,000 per offence and potential prosecution; linkage to annual return may block filing, triggering compliance default and strike-off risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue/asset size threshold in Alberta (ABCA) or under the CBCA. A statutory auditor is mandatory only for a distributing (public offering) corporation or where any shareholder holding 5% or more of the issued shares requisitions an audit; otherwise, a private non-distributing corporation can waive the audit annually by unanimous shareholder consent (ABCA s. 155(2); CBCA s. 161(1)). For a Tier-3/4 colocation lessor, external bank loan covenants or colocation customer contracts may require a filed audit engagement even where the audit is statutorily waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; private Canadian corporations typically adopt ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook – Part II). The T2 return reconciles statutory/net income to taxable income under the Income Tax Act; GST/HST remittances are governed by the Excise Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) under CBCA s. 21.3/21.4 and the Alberta BOT Act; update the register within 15 days of any direct/indirect share transfer or change in significant control; confirm the complete ISC list annually at the time of the Alberta annual return. A share transfer that changes a 25%-or-more owner, 25% voting right holder, or controlling shareholder must be recorded in the ISC register and reflected in the next annual registry confirmation; Alberta does not publicly disclose the filed RB information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (articles, by-laws, share transfers, and board/meeting resolutions)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300–900 (equivalent CAD 400–1,200) for Alberta registered office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 when audit waived by unanimous shareholder consent; 5,000–18,000 (CAD 7,000–25,000) for a covenant-driven or shareholder-requisitioned audit of a mid-sized colocation operating subsidiary; review engagement fallback 3,000–7,000 (CAD 4,000–9,500)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined (federal 15.0% + Alberta 8.0%); preferential 11.0% combined federal and Alberta rate on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (federal 9.0% + Alberta 2.0% on first CAD 500,000 for qualifying CCPC); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credit of 35% for qualifying CCPCs and 15% non-refundable for large corporations; accelerated Capital Cost Allowance under Class 50 (55% declining balance) for data-centre servers, racks and computer hardware; Class 1 (4%) and Class 8 (20%) CCA for building and cooling/power equipment; no Alberta capital tax for general corporations
